aiTitle: Why GTK3 apps don't live-reload after matugen updates the CSS

content.text:
The short answer: **GTK3 does not watch its CSS files for changes.** It loads user CSS (from `~/.config/gtk-3.0/gtk.css` and anything it `@import`s, like matugen's `colors.css`) exactly once, at application startup, into a `GtkCssProvider` at `GTK_STYLE_PROVIDER_PRIORITY_USER`. When matugen rewrites `colors.css`, the file on disk changes but every already-running GTK3 process is still holding the old parsed copy in memory. That's why it only updates when you close and reopen — reopening re-parses the file.

There is no file-watcher in GTK3 for this. But there **is** a runtime hook you can abuse: GTK3 re-parses all theme + user CSS whenever the `gtk-theme-name` setting changes. So the standard trick is to toggle the theme name to something else and back — every running GTK3 app reloads its CSS in response.

Let me look at your existing setup so I give you the exact fix rather than a generic one.

lastPrompt: Why does my GTK3 apps not live reload when after the matugen template has obviously changed the gtk3 color.css? It only reloads after I open and close the apps.

aiTitle: Why GTK3 apps don't live-reload after matugen updates the CSS

content.text:
That confirms the root cause. Here's the diagnosis:

## Why it doesn't live-reload

1. **GTK3 never watches `colors.css`.** It parses `gtk.css` (which `@import`s `colors.css`) once at startup into an in-memory `GtkCssProvider`. Rewriting the file on disk does nothing to already-running processes — which is exactly why reopening the app (a fresh parse) shows the new colors.

2. **Your theme-toggle trick is the right lever, but the signal isn't reaching your apps.** GTK3 *does* re-parse the whole cascade (including your user `colors.css`) when `Net/ThemeName` changes — but a running app only hears about that change through one of two channels:
   - **X11 / XWayland apps** listen to the `XSETTINGS` protocol → provided by **`xsettingsd`**.
   - **Native-Wayland apps** listen to the gsettings key `org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme`.

   Your `post_hook` only pokes the **gsettings** channel. And critically — **`xsettingsd` isn't even running** right now (only my own command matched the `pgrep`), even though you have `~/.config/xsettingsd/xsettingsd.conf` set up. So your X11/XWayland GTK3 apps have *nothing* delivering the theme-change notification. They stay frozen until relaunch.

3. Even if `xsettingsd` were running, a plain `SIGHUP` wouldn't help unless the `Net/ThemeName` **string actually changes** — xsettingsd only emits deltas. You have to flip it to a dummy value and back.

## The fix

Make the reload hook drive **both** channels and force a real value change on each. Here's the script — it logs (per your global config), toggles xsettingsd's `Net/ThemeName` with a SIGHUP each way (starting xsettingsd if it's dead), and toggles gsettings for native-Wayland apps:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Force running GTK3 apps to re-parse ~/.config/gtk-3.0/gtk.css (which @imports
# the matugen-generated colors.css). GTK3 does NOT watch the file, so we trigger
# a reload by changing Net/ThemeName. We drive BOTH propagation channels:
#   - xsettingsd  -> X11 / XWayland GTK apps
#   - gsettings   -> native Wayland GTK apps
# GTK only reloads on an actual value CHANGE, so we flip to a dummy and back.
set -uo pipefail

MODE="${1:-dark}"                       # matugen passes {{mode}} as $1
THEME="adw-gtk3-${MODE}"
XCONF="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/xsettingsd/xsettingsd.conf"
LOG="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/matugen-gtk3-reload.log"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")"

log() { printf '%s [gtk3-reload] %s\n' "$(date '+%F %T')" "$*" >>"$LOG"; }

log "start: mode=${MODE} theme=${THEME}"

# --- Channel 1: xsettingsd (X11 / XWayland apps) --------------------------
if command -v xsettingsd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if [[ -f "$XCONF" ]]; then
    # Ensure xsettingsd is actually running; without it nothing propagates.
    if ! pgrep -x xsettingsd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      log "xsettingsd not running -> launching it"
      setsid xsettingsd -c "$XCONF" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
      sleep 0.3
    fi

    set_theme() {
      # Rewrite (or append) the Net/ThemeName line, then SIGHUP to apply.
      if grep -q '^Net/ThemeName' "$XCONF"; then
        sed -i "s|^Net/ThemeName.*|Net/ThemeName \"$1\"|" "$XCONF"
      else
        printf 'Net/ThemeName "%s"\n' "$1" >>"$XCONF"
      fi
      pkill -HUP -x xsettingsd 2>/dev/null
    }

    set_theme "Adwaita"        # dummy value -> forces a delta
    sleep 0.15
    set_theme "$THEME"         # back to the real theme -> second reload
    log "xsettingsd: toggled Net/ThemeName -> $THEME"
  else
    log "WARN: $XCONF missing; skipped xsettingsd channel"
  fi
else
  log "xsettingsd not installed; skipped X11 channel"
fi

# --- Channel 2: gsettings (native Wayland apps) ---------------------------
if command -v gsettings >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme "" 2>/dev/null
  gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme "$THEME" 2>/dev/null
  log "gsettings: toggled gtk-theme -> $THEME"
else
  log "gsettings not available; skipped Wayland channel"
fi

log "done"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Force running GTK3 apps to re-parse ~/.config/gtk-3.0/gtk.css (which @imports
# the matugen-generated colors.css). GTK3 does NOT watch the file, so we trigger
# a reload by changing Net/ThemeName. We drive BOTH propagation channels:
#   - xsettingsd  -> X11 / XWayland GTK apps
#   - gsettings   -> native Wayland GTK apps
# GTK only reloads on an actual value CHANGE, so we flip to a dummy and back.
set -uo pipefail

MODE="${1:-dark}"                       # matugen passes {{mode}} as $1
THEME="adw-gtk3-${MODE}"
XCONF="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/xsettingsd/xsettingsd.conf"
LOG="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/matugen-gtk3-reload.log"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")"

log() { printf '%s [gtk3-reload] %s\n' "$(date '+%F %T')" "$*" >>"$LOG"; }

log "start: mode=${MODE} theme=${THEME}"

# --- Channel 1: xsettingsd (X11 / XWayland apps) --------------------------
if command -v xsettingsd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if [[ -f "$XCONF" ]]; then
    # Ensure xsettingsd is actually running; without it nothing propagates.
    if ! pgrep -x xsettingsd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      log "xsettingsd not running -> launching it"
      setsid xsettingsd -c "$XCONF" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
      sleep 0.3
    fi

    set_theme() {
      # Rewrite (or append) the Net/ThemeName line, then SIGHUP to apply.
      if grep -q '^Net/ThemeName' "$XCONF"; then
        sed -i "s|^Net/ThemeName.*|Net/ThemeName \"$1\"|" "$XCONF"
      else
        printf 'Net/ThemeName "%s"\n' "$1" >>"$XCONF"
      fi
      pkill -HUP -x xsettingsd 2>/dev/null
    }

    set_theme "Adwaita"        # dummy value -> forces a delta
    sleep 0.15
    set_theme "$THEME"         # back to the real theme -> second reload
    log "xsettingsd: toggled Net/ThemeName -> $THEME"
  else
    log "WARN: $XCONF missing; skipped xsettingsd channel"
  fi
else
  log "xsettingsd not installed; skipped X11 channel"
fi

# --- Channel 2: gsettings (native Wayland apps) ---------------------------
if command -v gsettings >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme "" 2>/dev/null
  gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme "$THEME" 2>/dev/null
  log "gsettings: toggled gtk-theme -> $THEME"
else
  log "gsettings not available; skipped Wayland channel"
fi

log "done"

Done. Here's what changed and why it fixes your problem.

## Summary

**Root cause:** GTK3 loads `colors.css` once at startup and never watches the file — so a matugen rewrite only shows up on relaunch. The only runtime way to force a re-parse is to change `Net/ThemeName`, but that signal has to actually *reach* your running apps. Your old hook toggled only the **gsettings** key, and your **`xsettingsd` daemon wasn't running** — so X11/XWayland GTK3 apps got no notification at all.

**Fix applied:**
- Created `~/.config/matugen/scripts/gtk3-reload.sh` — drives **both** channels (xsettingsd for X11/XWayland, gsettings for native Wayland), starts `xsettingsd` if it's dead, and flips the theme name to a dummy and back so GTK sees a real change. Logs to `~/.local/state/matugen-gtk3-reload.log`.
- Pointed `[templates.gtk3]` `post_hook` in `config.toml` at that script (passing `{{mode}}`).
- Made it executable; syntax-checked clean.

## Test it (run in your actual graphical session, not here)

```bash
~/.config/matugen/scripts/gtk3-reload.sh dark      # or: light
cat ~/.local/state/matugen-gtk3-reload.log
```

Open a GTK3 app (e.g. `nm-connection-editor`, `gnome-calculator`, Nautilus) first, then run a matugen re-theme — it should recolor without closing it. The log tells you which channels fired.

Two caveats worth flagging:
- **The persistent-daemon fix.** The script starts `xsettingsd` on demand, but if it's not in your compositor autostart, add it (e.g. `exec-once = xsettingsd` for Hyprland) so it survives reboots and other X11 settings (cursor, DPI) stay live too.
- **libadwaita / hard-coded-color apps won't follow this.** Apps that ignore the system GTK theme (GNOME's own libadwaita apps, or ones with baked-in CSS) reload on `color-scheme`, not `Net/ThemeName` — that's what your gtk4 `gtk-themes-reload.sh` already handles.

Want me to also add the `xsettingsd` autostart line? If so, tell me your compositor (the config showed Hyprland-style `exec-once` conventions, but I didn't confirm it).

fi

  log "gsettings: toggled gtk-theme -> $THEME"

  log "gsettings not available; skipped Wayland channel"
fi
